title: Finite-message characterization of public-coin complexity
statement: Fix an output type $\alpha$, a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, an error tolerance $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and a natural number $m$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist a coin-tape length $n \in \bbn$ and a public-coin finite-message protocol $p$ over the shared randomness $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ — that is, for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over the coin tape $\omega$ that $p$ outputs a value other than $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon$ — and the communication complexity of $p$ is at most $m$.
hypotheses_covered: existence of a finite-message public-coin protocol over CoinTape(n)
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
we have $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite-message public-coin protocol $p$ on
$\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$ and
$p.\mathrm{complexity} \le m$. This shows that the binary-message and
finite-message formulations of public-coin complexity coincide.
